rappel_detail.pull: A plumb pull off bolts. Keep the strands clear of the ledge lip and its trees so nothing catches on the retrieve.
rappel_detail.notes: Liberty Bell: Second station, on a large ledge reached by scrambling down and to the right from the first rappel.
hazards: Loose sand and grit on the ledge above slabby downclimbing.
If the chains are not found after the ropes are pulled, the party is stranded between stations with no anchor.
rappel_detail.station: Do not rappel straight on from the sandy ledge. Work right along the ledge, then down, then right again to reach a fixed station of bolts and chains on the steep wall. Parties consistently report this hardware as hard to spot, so scout it before pulling the first rope.

rappel_detail.pull: Because the rappel is diagonal, the pull strand drags across the wall and this descent has a documented history of jammed ropes. One party had to fix one strand, lead back up the climbable ground to free it, then ascend to the station and re-rig. Feed the pull strand out and away from the diagonal, and pull from the notch rather than from directly under the anchor.
rappel_detail.notes: Liberty Bell: Rappels somewhat diagonally into the Liberty Bell-Concord notch at about 7,300 ft. Downclimb the gully from there to the packs.
hazards: The line traverses, so anyone who loses the stance swings across the wall.
The notch and the gully below it are loose, and anything dislodged here funnels onto the climbers' path that other parties are walking up.
rappel_detail.station: The lowest fixed station on the wall, straight below the previous one. The rappel from it runs slightly diagonally rather than plumb and finishes in the Liberty Bell-Concord notch at roughly 7,300 ft, close to where most parties leave packs at the top of the approach gully.
The top of Concord Tower, on the south side toward Lexington Tower.
rappel_detail.notes: Concord Tower: Concord south face rappel 1 of 2, about 30 m on a single 60 m rope, to the bolted mid-face station.
hazards: Keep this south-face line distinct from Concord’s North Face rappels; their stations must not be mixed.

rappel_detail.station: The bolted station partway down Concord’s south face.
rappel_detail.notes: Concord Tower: Concord south face rappel 2 of 2, about 30 m, into the Concord-Lexington notch.

rappel_detail.anchor: anchor on Lexington Tower’s south face
rappel_detail.station: Top of Lexington Tower, on the south side.
rappel_detail.notes: Lexington Tower: rappel its south face; parties report one or two rappels here depending on where they break it.

rappel_detail.station: After crossing a short but exposed 3rd-class section beyond Lexington.
rappel_detail.notes: One more short rappel, then walk to the base of North Early Winters Spire.

rappel_detail.pull: About 22m. This is the only station on the line that is not a straight-down pull.
rappel_detail.notes: North Early Winters Spire, West Face: First rappel of the bolted West Face descent.
rappel_detail.anchor: bolted station or tree (~15ft/4-5m climber's-right of the route's top; accounts differ on whether tree or bolt comes first)
hazards: there are two separate rappel descents off this summit and old tat hangs above the other one, so it is possible to start down the wrong line
descriptions written before the face was bolted send you into the notch and gully instead, which is the slower and chossier option
rappel_detail.station: A bolted anchor in a comfortable alcove near the summit ridge, visible while you finish the last pitch. From the top of the third-class slabs the rappel goes back toward the West Face line, toward the climber's-right edge of the slabby ledge, to bolts just past the lip of the slab. Accounts differ on whether the top anchor is about 15 ft climber's right or climber's left of the finishing hand crack, so pick it out on the way up.

rappel_detail.pull: About 31m. The line is rigged for a single 70m; a 60m works but leaves no margin.
rappel_detail.notes: North Early Winters Spire, West Face: Bolts reported roughly every 100ft (~30m) down the West Face.
hazards: on a 60m rope the next anchor arrives at roughly waist height rather than at your feet — clippable, but knot the ends

rappel_detail.pull: About 32m. A 70m removes the problem entirely.
rappel_detail.notes: North Early Winters Spire, West Face: Continues down the bolted line.
hazards: this is the rappel that comes up short. Accounts split between blocking and extending one strand with about 5m of cord, reaching down to clip in and feeding rope through the device, and simply tying knots and finding it fine — the margin is small enough that rope stretch decides it, so plan the extension before you are hanging on it
rappel_detail.station: Bolted, straight down — the longest span on the line.

rappel_detail.pull: About 28m. Pulls on this line are reported as unusually clean — the bolts run down a blank, unclimbed section of face with little to snag on.
rappel_detail.notes: North Early Winters Spire, West Face: Continues down the bolted line.
hazards: some parties on a 60m report 10 to 20 ft of easy but very exposed downclimbing off the end of one of the middle rappels

rappel_detail.notes: North Early Winters Spire, West Face: Continues down the bolted line.
hazards: walk about 20m to the skier's-left end of the ledge, where a cairn and a short dirt path lead around a corner to the last station. Parties who miss it face a sandy, insecure downclimb instead, which is exactly what that last rappel exists to avoid
rappel_detail.station: Bolted, straight down to a big gravel and dirt ledge. The line breaks here: the next anchor is not below you.

rappel_detail.pull: About 28m to the ground, landing about a minute's walk from the base of the route and your packs.
rappel_detail.notes: North Early Winters Spire, West Face: Reaches the base near the packs; one party found a 60m rope just barely sufficient at one station.
rappel_detail.anchor: bolted station (lowest), or reportedly a tree for the final section
hazards: carry a little cord and a ring in case the tree is the only option and has been cleaned
rappel_detail.station: Around the corner at the end of the dirt ledge, on bolts just skier's left of a tree that is sometimes slung. Accounts differ on whether the last rappel goes from those bolts or from the tree itself, and at least one party found the tree's tat had been stripped.

rappel_detail.pull: Built for a single 60 m rope, and the stations were placed to give steep, clean pulls clear of the gully.
rappel_detail.notes: South Early Winters Spire, South Arete: First of three fixed rappel stations equipped in recent years on the South Arete; single 60m rope is sufficient for each rap.
rappel_detail.anchor: fixed bolt/chain station, climber's right of the summer gully/chimney
hazards: One party found one of these bolted stations placed on a large block that is not attached to the mountain: counted from the bottom it is the third, which with three stations in place is this top one, above the gully. Inspect the rock the bolts are in, not only the hardware, and back it up if you are not satisfied.
The short 5th-class step above the station is exposed with real fall consequence. Stay roped, and place gear on it rather than soloing down.
rappel_detail.station: Top station of the rappel line North Cascade Mountain Guides installed after the June 2022 rockfall: bolts and chains on a big ledge immediately above the small tree that older parties used to sling. All three new stations sit climber's right of the gully and off the line of ascent — skier's left as you face out on the way down — deliberately taking the descent out of the gully feature the route climbs. You reach it by downclimbing the arete's 3rd/4th-class ground plus one short, exposed 5th-class step.

rappel_detail.pull: Steep and fairly clean on a 60 m rope, provided the strands are kept out of the gully when you throw.
rappel_detail.notes: South Early Winters Spire, South Arete: Continues down the arete; short easy downclimbing sections connect stations.
hazards: The gully immediately beside the line is the loose ground that produced the 2022 rockfall. Keep ropes and feet out of it — that is the whole reason this rappel line was moved.
This is a very popular route and stations back up on summer weekends; anything knocked loose lands on the party waiting below.
rappel_detail.station: Second of the three chain-and-bolt stations, on the ledge just above the chockstone, again set off to the side of the climbing line. Short sections of easy downclimbing link it to the station above, and how much you rappel versus downclimb is a party choice.

rappel_detail.notes: South Early Winters Spire, South Arete: Final rappel returns to the base of the route.
hazards: Talus and slabs immediately below the last station, with the pull zone directly above anyone still coiling ropes.

The alternative descent some parties take instead — traversing to the Southwest Couloir and walking it out — avoids rope work but is loose and can hold firm snow well into summer, so it is not automatically the safer option without an axe.
rappel_detail.station: Lowest chain station. The rappel from it returns you to the base of the route, where the climbers' trail leads back down through talus and slabs alongside the stream to the Blue Lake Trail.

set.rappels: About 15 rappels across the day, spread over five summits: 2 from Liberty Bell into the Liberty Bell-Concord notch, 2 off Concord Tower’s south face, 1 or 2 off Lexington Tower plus one short one beyond it, 6 down North Early Winters Spire’s bolted West Face, and 3 off South Early Winters Spire’s South Arete.
set.rappel_count_note: Each summit’s rappels are listed in order, taken from that summit’s own descent. Lexington Tower is the one stretch without a published station list; parties report one or two rappels off its south face. A single 60 m rope covers everything except the bolted North Early Winters West Face line, which is rigged for a 70 m and only just works on a 60.
